one_sentence: The ten derived variables form five conjugate pairs via the Darboux theorem, forcing an Sp(10,R) symplectic structure whose subgroup chain recovers the Standard Model gauge group.
executive_summary: This document argues that the ten variables derived in Page 05 are not arbitrary but necessarily form five conjugate pairs due to the Darboux theorem in symplectic geometry. This pairing yields the symplectic group Sp(10,R), whose maximal compact subgroup U(5) quotients to SU(5), which then breaks via the Georgi-Glashow pattern to the Standard Model gauge group SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1). Three independent derivations—top-down from Trinitarian structure, bottom-up from the ten variables, and from scriptural mapping—converge on SU(5), suggesting a non-coincidental structural unity. The document also identifies an open problem: disambiguating the Casimir invariant of Sp(10,R).
short_summary: This document is a derivation of the symplectic structure of the ten variables from Page 05. The core structural claim is that the Darboux theorem forces five conjugate pairs, generating Sp(10,R) whose subgroup chain yields the Standard Model gauge group. Key evidence is the three-road convergence on SU(5) from independent theological, geometric, and scriptural starting points. This matters because it provides a unified geometric foundation for the Standard Model from first principles.
